title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issuing the Procedures for Pretrial Conferences in Criminal Cases Handled by People's Courts (Trial Implementation), the Procedures for Excluding Illegal Evidence in Criminal Cases Handled by People's Courts (Trial Implementation), and the Procedures for Court Investigation in Ordinary First Instance Proceedings for Criminal Cases Handled by People's Courts (Trial Implementation)
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Circular on Issuing the "Procedural Rules for Pre-Trial Conferences in Criminal Cases Handled by People's Courts (Trial Implementation)," "Procedural Rules for Excluding Illegally Obtained Evidence in Criminal Cases Handled by People's Courts (Trial Implementation)," and "Procedural Rules for Court Investigation in the Ordinary First Instance Procedure for Criminal Cases Handled by People's Courts (Trial Implementation)"

Fa Fa [2017] No. 31

To: The High People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the High People's Court of the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region; all intermediate people's courts nationwide, all theater and directly subordinate military courts, and all intermediate people's courts of the Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps:

To implement the "Opinions on Promoting the Reform of the Criminal Proceedings System Centered on Trial" and the "Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Strict Exclusion of Illegally Obtained Evidence in Criminal Cases" jointly issued by the Supreme People's Court, the Supreme People's Procuratorate, the Ministry of Public Security, the Ministry of State Security, and the Ministry of Justice, and to deepen the reform of the criminal proceedings system centered on trial, the Supreme People's Court has formulated the "Procedural Rules for Pre-Trial Conferences in Criminal Cases Handled by People's Courts (Trial Implementation)," the "Procedural Rules for Excluding Illegally Obtained Evidence in Criminal Cases Handled by People's Courts (Trial Implementation)," and the "Procedural Rules for Court Investigation in the Ordinary First Instance Procedure for Criminal Cases Handled by People's Courts (Trial Implementation)" (hereinafter referred to as the "Three Sets of Rules"), which are hereby issued to you for trial implementation as of January 1, 2018.

To better implement and enforce the "Three Sets of Rules" in judicial practice, the following requirements are put forward:

I. Fully recognize the significance of the "Three Sets of Rules." Promoting the reform of the criminal proceedings system centered on trial is a major reform deployment made at the Fourth Plenary Session of the 18th Central Committee of the Communist Party of China and a practical need to adhere to strict justice and ensure the fairness of criminal justice. The Supreme People's Court, the Supreme People's Procuratorate, the Ministry of Public Security, the Ministry of State Security, and the Ministry of Justice have successively issued the "Opinions on Promoting the Reform of the Criminal Proceedings System Centered on Trial" and the "Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Strict Exclusion of Illegally Obtained Evidence in Criminal Cases," putting forward an overall plan for reforming and improving the criminal proceedings system. To ensure the implementation and effectiveness of the central reform requirements and to optimize and improve trial procedures, especially court trial procedures, the Supreme People's Court, on the basis of issuing the "Implementation Opinions on Comprehensively Promoting the Reform of the Criminal Proceedings System Centered on Trial," has formulated the "Three Sets of Rules" to deepen the reform of substantive court trials. This will help to give full play to the decisive role of trials, especially court trials, in criminal proceedings and to build a more precise, standardized, and substantive criminal trial system. People's courts at all levels must fully recognize the significance of formulating the "Three Sets of Rules," accurately grasp the spirit of the reform, give full play to the functional role of trial procedures, and improve and implement legal principles and requirements such as adjudication based on evidence, exclusion of illegally obtained evidence, and giving the accused the benefit of the doubt in cases of doubt. Through the procedural fairness of court trials, the substantive fairness of case adjudications shall be achieved, enhancing judicial credibility.

II. Accurately grasp and implement the trial implementation requirements of the "Three Sets of Rules." Promoting the reform of the criminal proceedings system centered on trial involves the overall situation of political and legal work. People's courts at all levels must proactively report trial implementation work to Party committees and People's Congresses, maintain close communication and liaison with other political and legal organs, form a joint force for reform, and ensure steady progress in reform. They must promote the diversion of complex and simple cases, optimize the allocation of judicial resources, channel limited judicial resources into the trial of major, complex, and difficult cases, improve the fast-track procedure for criminal cases and the system of leniency for those who plead guilty and accept punishment, and achieve "meticulous trial of doubtful cases" and "speedy trial of simple cases." With a spirit of assuming responsibility and daring to take on accountability, they must strictly implement the principle of giving the accused the benefit of the doubt in cases of doubt, and lawfully declare acquittal in doubtful cases where the conviction evidence is insufficient, ensuring strict law enforcement and fair justice, and effectively preventing wrongful convictions. During the trial implementation period, people's courts at all levels, including the previously established pilot courts, must uniformly implement and enforce the relevant provisions of the "Three Sets of Rules" and must not act independently.

III. Strengthen the study and training for the "Three Sets of Rules." In formulating the "Three Sets of Rules," the Supreme People's Court has adhered to a problem-oriented and goal-oriented approach, focused on the central reform spirit and requirements, carefully summarized traditional trial experience, fully absorbed the results of previous reforms, and paid attention to concept innovation and institutional innovation. According to the Pre-Trial Conference Rules, at a pre-trial conference, a people's court may, in accordance with the law, handle procedural matters that might cause interruptions to the court trial, organize the prosecution and defense to present evidence, summarize the points of contention between the prosecution and defense, and clearly define the mechanism for connecting the pre-trial conference with the court trial. The Rules for Excluding Illegally Obtained Evidence focus on addressing the difficulties in initiating, proving, determining, and excluding illegally obtained evidence in the application of the exclusion procedure, further clarifying the specific rules and procedures for people's courts to review and exclude illegally obtained evidence. The Court Investigation Rules, based on summarizing traditional trial experience, establish adjudication based on evidence, procedural fairness, concentrated trial, and protection of procedural rights as the basic principles of court investigation, standardize the procedures for questioning and cross-examination at the opening of the trial, implement the system for witnesses, expert evaluators, and investigators to appear in court to testify, improve the rules for presenting, challenging, and admitting various types of evidence, and ensure that evidence is presented in court, facts of the case are ascertained in court, opinions of the prosecution and defense are expressed in court, and judgments are formed in court. High people's courts must attach great importance to and effectively supervise and urge people's courts in their jurisdictions to earnestly study the "Three Sets of Rules," carefully organize specialized training for criminal trial personnel, and ensure that every case handler can deeply understand the spirit and essence of the "Three Sets of Rules" and fully grasp their specific contents, so that they can effectively and skillfully apply them in specific work.

IV. Pay attention to summarizing and promoting the experience and practices of the trial implementation of the "Three Sets of Rules." People's courts at all levels should take the implementation of the "Three Sets of Rules" as an opportunity, focus on improving the rates of witnesses, expert evaluators, and investigators appearing in court to testify, the rate of defense lawyers, and the rate of judgments pronounced in court, and strive to advance the reform of the court trial system. They should strengthen communication and exchange between courts through field visits, court trial observations, and other means, share experiences, and improve together. They should adopt proactive and prudent methods, strengthen positive publicity and reporting, and create a favorable atmosphere for all parties to jointly promote reform. New situations and problems encountered during implementation, as well as new experiences and practices explored, should be carefully summarized and reported promptly level by level to the Supreme People's Court.

November 27, 2017

Procedural Rules for Pre-Trial Conferences in Criminal Cases Handled by People's Courts (Trial Implementation)

To implement the "Opinions on Promoting the Reform of the Criminal Proceedings System Centered on Trial" jointly issued by the Supreme People's Court, the Supreme People's Procuratorate, the Ministry of Public Security, the Ministry of State Security, and the Ministry of Justice, improve the pre-trial conference procedure, ensure focused and continuous court trials, and improve the quality and efficiency of court trials, these Rules are formulated in accordance with the law and in light of judicial practice.

Article 1: Where a people's court tries a criminal case using the ordinary procedure, and the case involves a large amount of evidentiary materials, complex and difficult facts, significant social impact, or substantial disputes between the prosecution and defense over facts and evidence, the court may decide to hold a pre-trial conference before the trial begins.

The prosecution or the defense may apply to the people's court to hold a pre-trial conference. Those applying to hold a pre-trial conference shall specify the matters to be addressed. If the people's court, upon review, deems it necessary, it shall decide to hold a pre-trial conference; if it decides not to hold a pre-trial conference, it shall inform the applicant of the decision.

If the defendant or the defense counsel applies before the trial to exclude illegally obtained evidence and provides relevant clues or materials in accordance with the law, the people's court shall hold a pre-trial conference.

Article 2: At a pre-trial conference, the people's court may inquire about matters related to the trial, hear opinions, and handle in accordance with the law matters such as withdrawal, the list of witnesses to appear in court, and the exclusion of illegally obtained evidence that may cause interruptions to the court trial; organize the prosecution and defense to present evidence; summarize the points of contention; and conduct mediation in the attached civil lawsuit.

Article 3: A pre-trial conference shall be presided over by the judge hearing the case; other members of the collegial panel may also preside over or participate in the pre-trial conference. Depending on the circumstances of the case, the judge hearing the case may direct a judge assistant to preside over the pre-trial conference.

The public prosecutor and the defense counsel shall participate in the pre-trial conference. Depending on the circumstances of the case, the defendant may participate in the pre-trial conference; if the defendant applies to participate in the pre-trial conference or applies to exclude illegally obtained evidence, the people's court shall notify the defendant to appear; in cases with multiple defendants, the presiding judge may determine, based on the circumstances of the case, which defendants shall participate in the pre-trial conference.

If the defendant applies to exclude illegally obtained evidence but does not have defense counsel, the people's court shall notify the legal aid agency to assign a lawyer to provide assistance to the defendant.

If mediation in the attached civil lawsuit is conducted during the pre-trial conference, the people's court shall notify the parties to the attached civil lawsuit to appear.

Article 4: If the defendant does not participate in the pre-trial conference, the defense counsel shall elicit the defendant's opinion on the matters to be addressed at the pre-trial conference before the conference is held.

Article 5: A pre-trial conference is generally not held in open court.

Depending on the circumstances of the case, a pre-trial conference may be conducted by video conference or other means.

Article 6: Depending on the circumstances of the case, a pre-trial conference may be held multiple times before the trial begins; after a trial is adjourned, a pre-trial conference may be held before the trial resumes.

Article 7: A pre-trial conference shall be held in the courtroom or other case-handling premises. If a defendant in custody participates, it may be held in the case-handling premises at the detention center.

If a defendant participates in the pre-trial conference, a judicial police officer shall be present.

Article 8: The people's court shall, based on the circumstances of the case and taking into account the opinions of the prosecution and defense, determine the matters to be addressed at the pre-trial conference, and notify the participants of the time, place, personnel, and matters of the conference three days before the conference is held. The notification shall be recorded in the case file.

If the defendant or the defense counsel applies before the trial to exclude illegally obtained evidence, the people's court shall, three days before the pre-trial conference is held, serve a copy of the application and the relevant clues or materials on the people's procuratorate.

Article 9: After the pre-trial conference begins, the presiding judge shall verify the attendance of participants and announce the matters to be addressed at the pre-trial conference.

If multiple defendants participate in the pre-trial conference and matters concerning facts and evidence are involved, the defendants shall be allowed to participate separately to prevent collusion of confessions.

Article 10: At a pre-trial conference, the presiding judge may inquire of the prosecution and defense and hear their opinions on the following matters:

(1) Whether there is an objection to the jurisdiction of the case;
(2) Whether there is an application for the withdrawal of relevant personnel;
(3) Whether there is an application for an in camera trial;
(4) Whether there is an application for the exclusion of illegally obtained evidence;
(5) Whether there is an application for the provision of new evidentiary materials;
(6) Whether there is an application for a new expert evaluation or inspection;
(7) Whether there is an application for the procurement of evidentiary materials proving the defendant's innocence or lesser guilt that were collected by the public security or procuratorial organs during investigation or review for prosecution but were not transferred with the case file;
(8) Whether there is an application for the collection or procurement of evidentiary materials from witnesses or relevant entities or individuals;
(9) Whether there is an application for witnesses, expert evaluators, investigators, or persons with specialized knowledge to appear in court, or whether there is an objection to the list of persons appearing in court;
(10) Other issues related to the trial.

For the matters specified in the preceding paragraph that may cause interruptions to the court trial, the people's court shall handle them in accordance with the law, inform the parties of the handling decision before the trial begins, and state the reasons. If the prosecution or defense raises the same application or objection again during the trial without new reasons, the court shall reject it in accordance with the law.

Article 11: If the defendant or the defense counsel raises an objection to the jurisdiction of the case, reasons shall be provided. If the people's court, upon review, finds the objection valid, it shall, in accordance with the law, return the case to the people's procuratorate or transfer it to the people's court with jurisdiction; if it finds that the court is not appropriate to exercise jurisdiction, it may request the higher-level people's court to handle the matter. If the people's court, upon review, finds the objection invalid, it shall reject it in accordance with the law.

Article 12: If the defendant or the defense counsel applies for the withdrawal of a judge, court clerk, interpreter, or expert evaluator, reasons shall be provided. If the people's court, upon review, finds the application valid, it shall decide the withdrawal of the relevant personnel in accordance with the law; if it finds the application invalid, it shall reject the application in accordance with the law.

If the defendant's or the defense counsel's application for withdrawal is rejected, they may apply for reconsideration once at the time of receiving the decision. If the circumstances do not fall within the provisions of Articles 28 or 29 of the Criminal Procedure Law, no reconsideration shall be allowed after the application for withdrawal is rejected.

If the defendant or the defense counsel applies for the withdrawal of a procurator, the people's court shall notify the people's procuratorate.

Article 13: If the defendant or the defense counsel applies for an in camera trial, and the people's court, upon review, finds that the case involves state secrets or personal privacy, it shall grant the application; if it finds that the case involves trade secrets, it may grant the application.

Article 14: If the defendant or the defense counsel applies before the trial to exclude illegally obtained evidence and provides relevant clues or materials in accordance with the law, the people's procuratorate shall, at the pre-trial conference, present relevant evidentiary materials or otherwise make a targeted explanation of the legality of the evidence collection. The people's court may verify the relevant evidentiary materials; upon application by the prosecution or defense, it may play targeted audio and video recordings of the interrogation.

The people's procuratorate may withdraw the relevant evidence; evidence that has been withdrawn shall not be presented at the trial without new reasons. The defendant or the defense counsel may withdraw the application for the exclusion of illegally obtained evidence; after withdrawal, they shall not apply again for the exclusion of the relevant evidence without new clues or materials.

If the prosecution and defense do not reach an agreement on the legality of the evidence collection at the pre-trial conference, the people's court shall conduct a court investigation. However, if the relevant evidentiary materials provided by the public prosecutor are indeed sufficient to exclude the possibility of illegal evidence collection, and there are no new clues or materials indicating that illegal evidence collection may have occurred, the presentation and challenge of evidence during the court investigation may be simplified.

Article 15: If the prosecution or defense applies for a new expert evaluation or inspection, reasons shall be provided. If the people's court, upon review, finds the reasons valid and the relevant evidentiary materials may affect the conviction or sentencing and cannot be remedied, it shall grant the application.

Article 16: If the defendant or the defense counsel applies in writing for the procurement of evidentiary materials proving the defendant's innocence or lesser guilt that were collected by the public security or procuratorial organs during investigation or review for prosecution but were not transferred with the case file, and provides relevant clues or materials, the people's court shall procure the materials and notify the people's procuratorate to transfer them within three days after receiving the procurement decision.

If the defendant or the defense counsel applies to collect or procure evidentiary materials from witnesses or relevant entities or individuals, reasons shall be provided. If the people's court, upon review, finds that the relevant evidentiary materials may affect the conviction or sentencing, it shall grant the application; if it finds that the relevant evidentiary materials are irrelevant to the case or are clearly redundant or unnecessary, it may deny the application.

Article 17: If the prosecution or defense applies for a witness, expert evaluator, investigator, or person with specialized knowledge to appear in court, reasons shall be provided. If the people's court, upon review, finds the reasons valid, it shall notify the relevant person to appear.

If the prosecution or defense objects to the list of witnesses, expert evaluators, investigators, or persons with specialized knowledge appearing in court, and the people's court, upon review, finds the objection valid, it shall handle the matter in accordance with the law; if it finds the objection invalid, it shall reject it in accordance with the law.

After notifying witnesses, expert evaluators, investigators, persons with specialized knowledge, or others to appear in court, the people's court shall inform the prosecution or defense to assist the relevant persons in appearing in court.

Article 18: Before a pre-trial conference is held, the people's procuratorate shall transfer all evidentiary materials to the people's court. The defendant and the defense counsel shall submit to the people's court all evidentiary materials they have collected proving the defendant's innocence, such as evidence that the defendant was not at the crime scene, had not reached the age of criminal responsibility, or was a mental patient who is not criminally responsible according to law.

After receiving the evidentiary materials transferred or submitted by the prosecution or defense, the people's court shall notify the other party to inspect, copy, or extract them.

Article 19: At a pre-trial conference, for evidence that the prosecution or defense decides to present at the trial, the people's court may organize the presentation of such evidence, hear the opinions of the prosecution and defense on the evidence in the case file, and sort out the disputed evidence.

For evidentiary materials on which the prosecution and defense have no dispute at the pre-trial conference, the presentation and challenge of evidence at the trial may be simplified.

If the people's court organizes the presentation of evidence, it shall generally notify the defendant to appear and hear the defendant's opinions; if the defendant does not appear, the defense counsel shall elicit the defendant's opinions before the pre-trial conference is held.

Article 20: The people's court may, at the pre-trial conference, summarize the points of contention between the prosecution and defense. Matters on which the prosecution and defense have no dispute or have reached an agreement may be tried in a simplified manner at the trial.

The people's court may organize the prosecution and defense to negotiate and determine the order and manner of presenting evidence at the trial, and clarify the method and focus of the court investigation. Matters on which no agreement is reached shall be determined by the people's court.

Article 21: Where the defendant does not plead guilty before the pre-trial conference but does plead guilty at the pre-trial conference, after verifying the voluntariness and authenticity of the defendant's guilty plea, the people's court may apply the fast-track procedure or the summary procedure in accordance with the law.

Article 22: After hearing the opinions of the prosecution and defense on the facts and evidence of the case at the pre-trial conference, if the facts are clearly unclear or the evidence is clearly insufficient, the people's court may recommend that the people's procuratorate supplement materials or withdraw the prosecution. If the people's procuratorate does not agree to the recommendation to withdraw the prosecution, and the people's court, after trial, has no new facts or reasons, it shall generally not permit the withdrawal of the prosecution.

Article 23: A record shall be made of the proceedings of the pre-trial conference, which shall be signed by the participants after verification.

After the pre-trial conference concludes, a pre-trial conference report shall be prepared, describing the basic circumstances of the pre-trial conference, the results of handling matters related to the trial, the points of contention between the prosecution and defense, and any agreements reached on relevant matters.

Article 24: In a case where a pre-trial conference has been held, after reading the indictment, the court shall announce the main contents of the pre-trial conference report; in cases involving multiple criminal acts, the relevant contents of the pre-trial conference report may be announced separately before the court investigation of the relevant criminal act begins; for matters such as jurisdiction objections, applications for withdrawal, or applications for in camera trial handled at the pre-trial conference, the court may announce the relevant contents of the pre-trial conference report after informing the parties of their litigation rights.

Article 25: After announcing the pre-trial conference report, for matters on which agreement was reached at the pre-trial conference, the court shall, after verifying with the prosecution and defense, confirm them in court; for matters on which no agreement was reached, the court may summarize the points of contention between the prosecution and defense, hear the opinions of the prosecution and defense, and handle the matter in accordance with the law.

If the prosecution or defense goes back on an agreement reached on a matter at the pre-trial conference during the trial, the court shall generally not address the matter again, unless there is a legitimate reason.

Article 26: Where a second instance people's court holds a pre-trial conference, the above provisions shall apply by reference.

Article 27: These Rules shall be effective on a trial basis as of January 1, 2018.

Procedural Rules for Excluding Illegally Obtained Evidence in Criminal Cases Handled by People's Courts (Trial Implementation)

To implement the "Opinions on Promoting the Reform of the Criminal Proceedings System Centered on Trial" and the "Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Strict Exclusion of Illegally Obtained Evidence in Criminal Cases," jointly issued by the Supreme People's Court, the Supreme People's Procuratorate, the Ministry of Public Security, the Ministry of State Security, and the Ministry of Justice, to standardize the procedure for excluding illegally obtained evidence, accurately punish crimes, effectively protect human rights, and effectively prevent wrongful convictions, these Rules are formulated in accordance with the law and in light of judicial practice.

Article 1: The following confessions of the defendant obtained by illegal methods shall be excluded:

(1) Confessions made against the defendant's will as a result of unbearable suffering inflicted by violent methods such as beating, illegal use of restraints, or harsh means constituting disguised corporal punishment;

(2) Statements obtained by subjecting the defendant to unbearable suffering and against his will through threats of violence or serious harm to the lawful rights and interests of the defendant or his close relatives;

(3) Statements of the defendant collected through illegal methods such as illegal detention that unlawfully restrict personal freedom.

Where a defendant makes a statement under torture, and thereafter makes repeated statements identical to the statement under the influence of such torture, such repeated statements shall also be excluded, except in the following circumstances:

(1) During the investigation stage, based on accusations, reports, or discovery by the investigative authority itself, if the investigative authority confirms or cannot rule out the collection of evidence through illegal methods, and after replacing the investigators, other investigators inform the defendant of his litigation rights and the legal consequences of confession during re-interrogation, and the defendant voluntarily makes a statement;

(2) During the stage of review of arrest, review of prosecution, and trial, if the prosecutor or judge informs the defendant of his litigation rights and the legal consequences of confession during interrogation, and the defendant voluntarily makes a statement.

Article 2: Witness testimony and victim statements obtained through illegal methods such as violence, threats, and illegal restriction of personal freedom shall be excluded.

Article 3: Physical evidence and documentary evidence collected through illegal methods such as illegal search and seizure in violation of statutory procedures, if they may seriously affect judicial fairness, shall be corrected or a reasonable explanation shall be provided; if correction or reasonable explanation cannot be provided, the relevant evidence shall be excluded.

Article 4: Illegally obtained evidence that is lawfully excluded shall not be read out, cross-examined, or used as a basis for adjudication.

Article 5: When a defendant and his defense counsel apply for exclusion of illegally obtained evidence, they shall provide relevant clues or materials. "Clues" refer to specific and targeted information regarding the persons, time, place, and methods of the suspected illegal evidence collection; "materials" refer to evidence such as photographs of injuries, medical examination records, hospital medical records, interrogation records, interrogation audio-video recordings, or testimony from cellmates that may reflect illegal evidence collection.

When a defendant and his defense counsel apply for exclusion of illegally obtained evidence, they shall submit a written application to the people's court. If the defendant has difficulty in writing, he may make an oral application, but it shall be recorded in the case file and signed or fingerprinted by the defendant.

Article 6: The burden of proof regarding the legality of evidence collection rests with the people's procuratorate.

If the people's procuratorate fails to provide evidence, or the evidence provided cannot prove the legality of evidence collection, and after court trial it is confirmed or cannot be ruled out that evidence was collected through illegal methods, the relevant evidence shall be excluded.

Article 7: Before the trial is opened, the presiding judge shall review the case file and examine the legality of evidence collection:

(1) Whether the defendant has applied for exclusion of illegally obtained evidence during the investigation or review of prosecution stage; if an application was made, whether relevant clues or materials were provided;

(2) Whether the investigative authority or the people's procuratorate has investigated and verified the legality of evidence collection; if investigation and verification were conducted, whether a conclusion was made;

(3) For major cases, whether the procuratorial officer stationed at the detention center has verified the legality of interrogation before the conclusion of investigation, and whether synchronized audio-video recording of the verification process was made; if verification was conducted, whether a conclusion was made;

(4) Whether evidence excluded by the people's procuratorate as illegally obtained during the review of arrest or review of prosecution stage has been transferred with the case file and clearly identified as excluded illegally obtained evidence.

After examining the legality of evidence collection, if the people's court finds that additional evidence materials are needed, it shall notify the people's procuratorate to supplement them within three days.

Article 8: When serving a copy of the indictment to the defendant and his defense counsel, the people's court shall inform them of their right to apply for exclusion of illegally obtained evidence before the trial and to provide relevant clues or materials at the same time. The above circumstances shall be recorded in the case file.

If the defendant applies for exclusion of illegally obtained evidence but has no defense counsel, the people's court shall notify a legal aid institution to appoint a lawyer to provide defense for him.

Article 9: The defendant and his defense counsel shall apply for exclusion of illegally obtained evidence before the trial, except where relevant clues or materials are discovered during the trial.

Article 10: If the defendant and his defense counsel apply for exclusion of illegally obtained evidence and provide relevant clues or materials, the people's court shall convene a pre-trial conference, and shall send copies of the application and relevant clues or materials to the people's procuratorate three days before the pre-trial conference.

If the defendant and his defense counsel apply for exclusion of illegally obtained evidence but fail to provide relevant clues or materials, the people's court shall notify them to supplement them. If the defendant and his defense counsel fail to supplement, the people's court shall not accept the application and shall inform the defendant and his defense counsel before the trial. The above circumstances shall be recorded in the case file.

Article 11: For major cases where the defendant may be sentenced to life imprisonment, death penalty, or for organized crime of a triad nature, serious drug crimes, etc., if the defendant, when questioned by the procuratorial officer stationed at the detention center about the legality of interrogation, explicitly states that there was no torture or other illegal evidence collection during the investigation stage, but later applies for exclusion of illegally obtained evidence during the trial stage, he shall provide reasons. If the people's court, upon review, has no doubt about the legality of evidence collection, it may dismiss the application.

If the procuratorial officer stationed at the detention center fails to verify the legality of interrogation before the conclusion of investigation in a major case, or fails to make a synchronized audio-video recording of the entire verification process, and the defendant and his defense counsel apply for exclusion of illegally obtained evidence during the trial stage, providing relevant clues or materials, and the people's court has doubts about the legality of evidence collection, it shall conduct an investigation according to law.

Article 12: In a pre-trial conference, when the people's court examines the legality of evidence collection, it generally follows the following steps:

(1) The defendant and his defense counsel explain the application for exclusion of illegally obtained evidence and the relevant clues or materials;

(2) The public prosecutor provides evidence materials proving the legality of evidence collection;

(3) The prosecution and defense express opinions on the legality of evidence collection;

(4) If the prosecution and defense fail to reach agreement on the legality of evidence collection, the trial judge summarizes the disputed issues.

Article 13: In a pre-trial conference, the people's procuratorate shall, by presenting relevant evidence materials and other means, specifically explain the legality of evidence collection. The people's court may verify the relevant materials, and upon application by the prosecution or defense, may play interrogation audio-video recordings in a targeted manner.

Article 14: In a pre-trial conference, the people's procuratorate may withdraw relevant evidence. Withdrawn evidence shall not be presented at trial without new reasons.

The defendant and his defense counsel may withdraw the application for exclusion of illegally obtained evidence. After withdrawing the application, unless new clues or materials emerge, they may not apply again for exclusion of the relevant evidence.

Article 15: If the prosecution and defense reach an agreement on the legality of evidence collection at the pre-trial conference, the court shall verify with the prosecution and defense at trial and confirm it in court. If one party reneges at trial, unless there are legitimate reasons, the court generally will not conduct further review.

If the prosecution and defense fail to reach an agreement on the legality of evidence collection at the pre-trial conference, the people's court shall conduct an investigation at trial; however, if the relevant evidence materials provided by the public prosecutor are indeed sufficient to rule out illegal evidence collection, and there are no new clues or materials indicating possible illegal evidence collection, the trial investigation, presentation of evidence, and cross-examination may be simplified.

Article 16: The trial judge shall include in the pre-trial conference report a description of the review of the legality of evidence collection, mainly including the disputed issues between the prosecution and defense and the matters on which agreement was reached.

Article 17: If the defendant and his defense counsel did not apply for exclusion of illegally obtained evidence before the trial but make an application during the trial, they shall provide reasons. If the people's court, upon review, has doubts about the legality of evidence collection, it shall conduct an investigation; if there are no doubts, it shall dismiss the application.

After the people's court dismisses the application for exclusion of illegally obtained evidence, if the defendant and his defense counsel apply again on the same grounds without new clues or materials, the people's court shall not review it again.

Article 18: If the people's court decides to conduct a court investigation into the legality of evidence collection, it shall conduct the investigation first during the trial. For circumstances such as where the evidence subject to exclusion is unrelated to other criminal facts, to avoid excessive delay of the trial, the court may first investigate other criminal facts and then investigate the legality of evidence collection.

Before the conclusion of the court investigation procedure on the legality of evidence collection, the relevant evidence shall not be read out or cross-examined.

Article 19: When the court decides to investigate the legality of evidence collection, it generally follows the following steps:

(1) For cases where a pre-trial conference has been held, after reading the indictment, the court shall announce the results of the review of the legality of evidence collection at the pre-trial conference and the disputed issues between the prosecution and defense;

(2) The defendant and his defense counsel explain the application for exclusion of illegally obtained evidence and the relevant clues or materials;

(3) The public prosecutor presents evidence materials proving the legality of evidence collection, and the defendant and his defense counsel may cross-examine the relevant evidence; with the permission of the presiding judge, the public prosecutor and defense counsel may question the investigators or other persons who appear in court;

(4) The prosecution and defense debate on the legality of evidence collection.

Article 20: To prove the legality of evidence collection, the public prosecutor may present evidence materials such as interrogation records, interrogation registration forms, medical examination records, legal documents for compulsory measures or investigative measures, and materials verifying the legality of interrogation before the conclusion of investigation; and may also play interrogation audio-video recordings for the interrogation period objected to by the defendant and his defense counsel, and request the court to notify investigators or other persons to appear in court to explain the situation. Written explanations signed and sealed by investigators shall not replace the appearance of investigators in court.

During the trial, if the public prosecutor is unable to present evidence or needs to supplement investigation for new evidence and proposes an adjournment, the court may agree.

Article 21: The defendant and his defense counsel may present relevant clues or materials and apply for the court to play interrogation audio-video recordings for a specific interrogation period.

If the defendant and his defense counsel apply to the people's court to obtain interrogation audio-video recordings, medical examination records, and other evidence materials collected but not submitted by the investigative authority or the people's procuratorate, and the people's court, upon review, finds that such evidence materials are related to the legality of evidence collection, it shall obtain them; if it finds that they are unrelated to the legality of evidence collection, it shall decide not to obtain them and explain the reasons to the defendant and his defense counsel.

If the defendant and his defense counsel apply for the people's court to notify investigators or other persons to appear in court to explain the situation, and the people's court finds it truly necessary, it may notify the above persons to appear in court.

Article 22: When the court investigates the legality of evidence collection, it shall attach importance to the review of interrogation audio-video recordings, focusing on the following:

(1) Whether the interrogation audio-video recordings were made according to law. For cases where the defendant may be sentenced to life imprisonment, death penalty, or other major criminal cases, whether the interrogation process was recorded by audio-video;

(2) Whether the interrogation audio-video recordings are complete. Whether each interrogation session was recorded by audio-video, whether the recording was uninterrupted throughout, and whether there were situations such as selective recording, editing, or deletion;

(3) Whether the interrogation audio-video recordings were made synchronously. Whether the recording was made from the start of the interrogation until after the criminal suspect reviewed the interrogation record and signed to confirm; whether the start and end times recorded in the interrogation record match the times reflected in the interrogation audio-video recording;

(4) Whether there are discrepancies between the interrogation audio-video recording and the content of the interrogation record. For content related to conviction and sentencing, whether there are substantive discrepancies between the content recorded in the interrogation record and the interrogation audio-video recording; if there are substantive discrepancies, the interrogation audio-video recording shall prevail.

Article 23: When investigators or other persons appear in court, they shall explain the process of evidence collection to the court and answer questions regarding the relevant circumstances. If the manner of questioning is improper or the content is unrelated to the legality of evidence collection, the court shall stop it.

If, after being notified by the people's court, investigators do not appear in court to explain the situation, and it cannot be ruled out that evidence was collected through illegal methods, the relevant evidence shall be excluded.

Article 24: If the people's court has doubts about the source or content of evidence provided by the prosecution or defense, it may inform the prosecution or defense to supplement evidence or provide explanations; if necessary, it may adjourn the court to investigate and verify the evidence. When investigating and verifying evidence outside court, the court may notify the prosecution and defense to be present, and the verification process shall be recorded in the case file.

Evidence supplemented by the prosecution or defense and evidence obtained through out-of-court investigation and verification by the court, if not verified as true through court investigation procedures such as presentation and cross-examination, shall not be used as a basis for proving the legality of evidence collection.

Article 25: After investigating the legality of evidence collection, the people's court shall make a decision in court on whether to exclude the relevant evidence. If necessary, it may adjourn the court for the collegial panel to deliberate or submit to the adjudication committee for discussion, and announce the decision when the court resumes.

Article 26: After trial, if any of the following circumstances exist, the relevant evidence shall be excluded:

(1) It is confirmed that evidence was collected through illegal methods;

(2) For cases where interrogation audio-video recording should have been made, no interrogation audio-video recording was provided, or the interrogation audio-video recording has selective recording, editing, deletion, etc., and the existing evidence cannot rule out that evidence was collected through illegal methods;

(3) The investigative authority interrogated outside the designated case-handling place without emergency, and the existing evidence cannot rule out that evidence was collected through illegal methods;

(4) The procuratorial officer stationed at the detention center failed to verify the legality of interrogation before the conclusion of investigation in a major case, or failed to make a synchronized audio-video recording of the verification process, or the audio-video recording has selective recording, editing, deletion, etc., and the existing evidence cannot rule out that evidence was collected through illegal methods;

(5) Other circumstances where it cannot be ruled out that evidence was collected through illegal methods.

Article 27: The procedures for the people's court to review and investigate the legality of evidence collection of witness testimony, victim statements, physical evidence, documentary evidence, etc., shall refer to the above provisions.

Article 28: The conclusions of the people's court's review and investigation of the legality of evidence collection shall be stated in the judgment document, with reasons provided.

Article 29: If the people's procuratorate, the defendant, or his legal representative files a protest or appeal, disputing the first-instance people's court's review and investigation conclusions on the legality of evidence collection, the second-instance people's court shall review it.

Article 30: If the defendant and his defense counsel did not apply for exclusion of illegally obtained evidence in the first-instance proceedings but make an application in the second-instance proceedings, and any of the following circumstances exists, the second-instance people's court shall review it:

(1) The first-instance people's court failed to inform the defendant of his right to apply for exclusion of illegally obtained evidence according to law;

(2) The defendant and his defense counsel discovered relevant clues or materials suspected of illegal evidence collection after the first-instance trial.

Article 31: The people's procuratorate shall comprehensively present evidence materials proving the legality of evidence collection in the first-instance proceedings.

If the people's procuratorate fails to present evidence proving the legality of evidence collection in the first-instance proceedings, and the first-instance people's court lawfully excludes the relevant evidence, the people's procuratorate shall not present the previously unpresented evidence in the second-instance proceedings, except where such evidence was discovered after the first-instance proceedings.

Article 32: The investigation of the legality of evidence collection by the second-instance people's court shall refer to the provisions on the first-instance procedures above.

Article 33: If the first-instance people's court fails to review the application of the defendant and his defense counsel for exclusion of illegally obtained evidence and uses the relevant evidence as a basis for adjudication, which may affect the fairness of the trial, the second-instance people's court shall rule to set aside the original judgment and remand the case to the original trial people's court for retrial.

Article 34: If the first-instance people's court fails to exclude illegally obtained evidence that should be excluded according to law, the second-instance people's court may exclude the relevant evidence according to law. After excluding the illegally obtained evidence, it shall make a decision according to the following circumstances:

(1) If the original judgment correctly finds the facts and applies the law and the sentence is appropriate, it shall rule to dismiss the appeal or protest and affirm the original judgment;

(2) If the original judgment finds the facts correctly but the application of the law is erroneous or the sentence is inappropriate, it shall amend the judgment;

(3) If the facts in the original judgment are unclear or the evidence is insufficient, it may amend the judgment after clarifying the facts, or rule to set aside the original judgment and remand the case to the original trial people's court for retrial.

Article 35: The review and investigation of the legality of evidence collection in retrial procedures and death penalty review procedures shall refer to the above provisions.

Article 36: These Procedures shall be implemented on a trial basis from January 1, 2018.

People's Court Procedures for Handling Criminal Cases

Court Investigation Procedures for Ordinary First-Instance Trials (Trial)

To implement the "Opinions on Advancing Criminal Procedure System Reform Centered on Trials" issued by the Supreme People's Court, Supreme People's Procuratorate, Ministry of Public Security, Ministry of State Security, and Ministry of Justice, to standardize court investigation procedures, improve trial quality and efficiency, and ensure that evidence is presented, facts are found, opinions are expressed, and adjudications are made in court, these Procedures are formulated in accordance with legal provisions and in light of judicial practice.

Part I: General Provisions

Article 1: The court shall adhere to the principle of evidence-based adjudication. Determination of case facts must be based on evidence. Court investigation shall be centered on the examination of evidence. Illegally obtained evidence that the court determines and lawfully excludes shall not be read out or cross-examined. Evidence that has not been verified as true through court investigation procedures such as presentation, reading out, identification, and cross-examination shall not be used as a basis for adjudication.

Article 2: The court shall adhere to the principle of procedural fairness. The people's procuratorate bears the burden of proving the defendant's guilt according to law; the defendant does not bear the burden of proving his innocence. The court shall adjudicate neutrally, strictly implement statutory trial procedures, ensure equal confrontation between the prosecution and defense in the court investigation stage, and achieve substantive justice in case adjudication through procedural fairness in trials.

Article 3: The court shall adhere to the principle of concentrated trial. Standardize pre-trial preparation procedures to avoid unnecessary delays and interruptions during trial. The presiding judge shall review the case file before trial, determine the trial plan, and report to the collegial panel on the preparation status for trial. For cases where a pre-trial conference has been held, the court may handle matters that may cause interruption of the trial according to law, organize the prosecution and defense to present evidence, and summarize the disputed issues between the prosecution and defense.

Article 4: The court shall adhere to the principle of protection of litigation rights. Lawfully protect the rights of the parties and other litigation participants to be informed, to make statements, to debate and defend, to apply, and to appeal; protect the rights of defense counsel to question, cross-examine, debate, and defend; and improve working mechanisms to facilitate defense counsel's participation in litigation.

Part II: Procedures for Opening the Court and Questioning

Article 5: After the court opens the session, it shall inform the parties of the litigation rights available to them under law during the trial.

For cases where a pre-trial conference has been held and litigation rights matters were dealt with in the pre-trial conference, the court may, during the session of informing the parties of their litigation rights after the opening, also announce the results of the handling of relevant matters in the pre-trial conference.

Article 6: After the public prosecutor reads the indictment, for cases where a pre-trial conference has been held, the court shall announce the main content of the pre-trial conference report. Where there are multiple criminal facts, the court may, at the beginning of the court investigation on the relevant criminal facts, separately announce the relevant content of the pre-trial conference report.

For matters on which consensus has been reached during the pre-trial conference, the court may, after verification with the prosecution and defense, confirm them in court. For matters on which no consensus has been reached, the court may, during the segment of the trial involving such matters, summarize the points of dispute, hear the opinions of the prosecution and defense, and render a decision in accordance with the law.

Article 7. After the prosecutor reads the indictment, the presiding judge shall ask the defendant whether he or she has any objection to the criminal facts alleged in the indictment, and shall hear the defendant’s statements and explanations. If the defendant pleads guilty in court, the court shall verify the voluntariness and truthfulness of the plea and hear the defendant’s statements and explanations.

Under the direction of the presiding judge, the prosecutor may interrogate the defendant regarding the criminal facts alleged in the indictment. To avoid undue delay of the trial, questioning of the defendant on evidentiary issues may be conducted during the stage of presenting and examining evidence. With the permission of the presiding judge, the victim and his or her statutory agent or agent ad litem may supplement the questioning on the criminal facts that were the subject of the prosecutor’s interrogation; the plaintiff in the incidental civil action and his or her statutory agent or agent ad litem may question the defendant regarding the facts of the incidental civil part; the defendant’s statutory agent or defense counsel, and the defendant in the incidental civil action and his or her statutory agent or agent ad litem may question the defendant after the prosecuting party has concluded its questioning on a particular issue. In cases with multiple defendants, questioning of the defendant by defense counsel shall be conducted under the direction of the presiding judge, first by the defense counsel of the defendant in question, and then by the defense counsel of other defendants.

Article 8. In cases involving multiple defendants, the interrogation of each defendant shall be conducted separately.

If there are material inconsistencies among the statements of the defendants, the court may summon the relevant defendants to appear in court for confrontation. The presiding judge may separately interrogate the defendants to investigate and verify the material inconsistencies in their statements. With the permission of the presiding judge, the prosecution and defense may interrogate or question the defendants. If the presiding judge deems it necessary, the defendants may be permitted to question each other.

Based on the needs of the trial, the presiding judge may arrange for the defendants to confront witnesses or victims in accordance with the method prescribed in the preceding paragraph.

Article 9. If there are numerous victims who apply to participate in the trial, and the case does not fall within the scope of an incidental civil action, the victims may elect several representatives to participate in or observe the trial, and the People's Court may also designate representatives.

After the interrogation and questioning of the defendant have been concluded and before the presentation of other evidence, under the direction of the presiding judge, the victims participating in the trial may make statements regarding the criminal facts alleged in the indictment. With the permission of the presiding judge, the prosecution and defense may question the victims after their statements.

Article 10. To resolve doubts concerning the defendant’s statements and explanations, the judicial personnel may interrogate the defendant or may question the victims or the parties to the incidental civil action.

Article 11. In cases involving multiple criminal facts, the court investigation regarding facts for which the defendant does not plead guilty shall generally be conducted separately.

In cases where the defendant does not plead guilty or pleads guilty but later retracts the plea, the court shall conduct a comprehensive investigation of all facts and evidence relevant to conviction and sentencing.

In cases where the defendant pleads guilty in court, after verifying the voluntariness and truthfulness of the plea and confirming that the defendant is aware of the legal consequences of such a plea, the court may focus the investigation on sentencing facts and other disputed issues.

III. Procedures for Witness Testimony in Court

Article 12. The prosecution and defense may apply to the court to notify witnesses, expert witnesses, investigators, or persons with specialized knowledge to appear in court.

The victim and his or her statutory agent or agent ad litem, and the plaintiff in the incidental civil action and his or her agent ad litem may also file such applications.

Article 13. If the prosecution or defense objects to witness testimony or victim statements and applies for the witness or victim to appear in court, and the People's Court, upon review, finds that the witness testimony or victim statements have a significant impact on the conviction and sentencing of the case, it shall notify the witness or victim to appear in court.

If the prosecution or defense objects to an expert opinion and applies for the expert witness or a person with specialized knowledge to appear in court, and the People's Court, upon review, deems it necessary, it shall notify the expert witness or the person with specialized knowledge to appear in court.

If the prosecution or defense objects to the process of case solving, the source of evidence, the authenticity of evidence, or the legality of evidence collection, and applies for an investigator or relevant personnel to appear in court, and the People's Court, upon review, deems it necessary, it shall notify the investigator or relevant personnel to appear in court.

To ascertain the facts of the case or to investigate and verify evidence, the People's Court may, on its own authority, notify the above-mentioned persons to appear in court.

If the People's Court notifies witnesses, victims, expert witnesses, investigators, persons with specialized knowledge, or others to appear in court, the prosecution and defense shall assist such persons in appearing.

Article 14. If a witness who is required to testify in court is genuinely unable to appear due to objective reasons such as a serious illness during the trial, he or she may testify through video or other means.

When a witness testifies by video, the procedures for questioning and examining evidence shall be conducted by reference to the procedures for witness testimony in court.

The provisions of the preceding paragraph apply to victims, expert witnesses, and investigators.

Article 15. If a witness notified by the People's Court to appear in court refuses to do so without justifiable reasons, the court may compel his or her appearance, except for the spouse, parents, or children of the defendant.

To compel a witness to appear in court, the president of the court shall issue an order for compulsory appearance, executed by judicial police. If necessary, the court may request the assistance of the public security authorities.

Article 16. If the personal safety of a witness, expert witness, or victim testifying in court, or of his or her close relatives, is in danger, the People's Court shall take protective measures such as not disclosing personal information including the true name, address, and work unit, or not revealing their appearance or true voice.

If a decision is made to take protective measures of not disclosing personal information for a witness, expert witness, or victim testifying in court, the judicial personnel shall verify their identities before the trial opens; the affidavit of the witness or expert witness to testify truthfully shall not be disclosed, and in judgments, rulings, and other legal documents, pseudonyms may be used in place of their personal information.

During the trial, if a witness, expert witness, or victim requests protection, the People's Court shall immediately review the request and, if genuinely necessary, shall promptly decide to take corresponding protective measures. If necessary, the court may request the public security authorities to take specialized protective measures.

Article 17. Reasonable expenses such as transportation, meals, and accommodation incurred by witnesses, expert witnesses, and persons with specialized knowledge for testifying in court, except for those paid by the prosecution or defense, shall be included in the special fund for subsidies for testifying in court and shall be disbursed by the People's Court in accordance with prescribed procedures after their testimony.

Article 18. When witnesses or expert witnesses appear in court, the court shall, in court, verify their identity and their relationship with the parties and the case, examine their capacity to testify and professional qualifications, and inform them of their rights, obligations, and legal liabilities concerning testimony.

Before testifying, witnesses and expert witnesses shall guarantee to provide truthful testimony or explain their expert opinions to the court and shall sign an affidavit.

Article 19. After a witness appears in court, he or she shall first make a statement to the court. Then the party presenting the witness shall first ask questions; after the questioning is concluded, the opposing party may also ask questions. Based on the needs of the trial, the questioning may also be conducted first by the applying party.

After the prosecution and defense have concluded their questioning of the witness, they may present their opinions on the examination of the witness’s testimony. If the prosecution or defense has new questions, they may, with the permission of the presiding judge, question the witness again.

When the judicial personnel deem it necessary, they may question the witness. In cases where the court notifies a witness to appear on its own authority, the judicial personnel shall lead the questioning of the witness. With the permission of the presiding judge, the defendant may question the witness.

Article 20. Questioning of witnesses shall comply with the following rules:

(1) The content of the questions shall be relevant to the facts of the case;
(2) Leading questions shall not be used;
(3) Witnesses shall not be threatened or misled;
(4) The personal dignity of witnesses shall not be impaired;
(5) The personal privacy of witnesses shall not be disclosed.

Article 21. If one party’s method of questioning is improper or the content of the questions is irrelevant to the facts of the case, violating the relevant rules of questioning, the opposing party may raise an objection. If the opposing party raises an objection in court, the questioning party shall explain the reason for the question; the presiding judge shall determine the situation and either sustain or overrule the objection. If the opposing party does not raise an objection in court, the presiding judge may also stop the questioning based on the circumstances.

Article 22. If the presiding judge finds that the content of a witness’s statement in court is irrelevant to the facts of the case or is clearly repetitive, he or she may give necessary reminders.

Article 23. In cases where multiple witnesses testify in court, questioning of the witnesses shall be conducted separately.

When multiple witnesses appear in court to testify, they shall wait at a location designated by the court and shall not discuss the case; if necessary, measures such as isolated waiting may be taken. After a witness has testified in court, the presiding judge shall notify the judicial police to guide the witness out of the courtroom. Witnesses shall not observe the trial of the case.

If a victim is not listed as a party to participate in the trial but only appears in court to state the facts of the case, the provisions of the preceding paragraph shall apply by reference.

Article 24. If there are material differences among the testimony of witnesses, the court may summon the relevant witnesses to appear in court for confrontation.

The presiding judge may separately question the witnesses to investigate and verify the material differences in their testimony. With the permission of the presiding judge, the prosecution and defense may question the witnesses. If the presiding judge deems it necessary, the witnesses may be permitted to question each other.

Article 25. If a witness testifies in court, his or her pre-trial testimony shall generally not be presented or read out in court, except in the following circumstances:

(1) When the witness, while testifying in court, forgets or omits key content of the pre-trial testimony, and necessary reminders need to be given to the witness;
(2) When the witness’s testimony in court contradicts the pre-trial testimony, and the witness needs to provide a reasonable explanation.

To verify the source of evidence, the authenticity of evidence, or other issues, or to assist the witness in recalling, the prosecution and defense may, with the permission of the presiding judge, present physical evidence, documentary evidence, or other evidence to the witness while questioning him or her.

Article 26. The prosecution and defense may apply to the court to notify a person with specialized knowledge to appear in court to assist their side in examining expert opinions during cross-examination. The person with specialized knowledge may appear in court simultaneously with the expert witness, question the expert witness after the expert witness has testified, and provide opinions on specialized issues in the case.

An application for a person with specialized knowledge to appear in court shall include a list of such persons and shall not exceed two persons. In cases involving multiple types of expert opinions, the number of persons may be increased accordingly.

Article 27. The questioning of victims, expert witnesses, investigators, and persons with specialized knowledge shall be conducted by reference to the relevant provisions concerning witnesses.

If the same expert opinion is rendered by multiple expert witnesses, the relevant expert witnesses and the person with specialized knowledge who examines that expert opinion during cross-examination may appear in court simultaneously, without being subject to the restriction of separate questioning rules.

IV. Procedures for Presenting and Examining Evidence

Article 28. After the opening interrogation and questioning have been concluded, the prosecutor shall first present evidence. After the prosecutor has concluded presenting evidence, the defendant and his or her defense counsel shall present evidence.

After the prosecutor presents evidence, with the permission of the presiding judge, the defendant and his or her defense counsel may present relevant evidence to rebut it.

After one party presents evidence, the opposing party may present opinions on the examination of the evidence. If necessary, the prosecution and defense may conduct multiple rounds of examining disputed evidence.

If the defendant and his or her defense counsel believe that certain evidence presented by the prosecutor is favorable to their own litigation claims, they may acknowledge it when presenting their opinions on the examination of the evidence, or directly cite the relevant evidence when presenting their defense arguments.

Article 29. For evidence that the prosecution or defense has submitted along with the case file or submitted before trial but has not presented in court, the presiding judge may give necessary reminders. For key evidence among such evidence that may affect conviction and sentencing, the presiding judge shall remind the prosecution and defense to present it.

If there are doubts concerning facts or evidence that may affect conviction and sentencing in the case, and the prosecution and defense have not mentioned them, the presiding judge shall guide the prosecution and defense to present their opinions on the examination of the evidence and shall investigate and verify them in accordance with the law.

Article 30. The court shall attach importance to the review of the legality of evidence collection. If there are doubts about the legality of evidence collection, the court shall investigate and verify the evidentiary materials that prove the legality of the collection.

If the defendant and his or her defense counsel apply for the exclusion of illegally obtained evidence and provide relevant leads or materials in accordance with the law, and the court has doubts about the legality of evidence collection and decides to conduct an investigation, the investigation shall generally be conducted first and in court.

Article 31. For key evidence that may affect conviction and sentencing and evidence disputed by the prosecution and defense, it shall generally be presented and examined separately, and opinions on the examination of the evidence shall be fully heard.

For non-key evidence that is not disputed by the prosecution and defense, the party presenting the evidence may merely explain the name of the evidence and the facts it proves, and the opposing party may present opinions on the examination of the evidence.

For cases in which a pre-trial conference was held, the presentation and examination of evidence may be conducted in the manner determined at the pre-trial conference. Based on the needs of the trial, the court may give necessary reminders regarding the manner of presenting and examining evidence by the prosecution and defense.

Article 32. For physical evidence, documentary evidence, audio-visual materials, electronic data, and other evidence, the original object or original document shall be presented. If it is genuinely difficult to obtain the original object or original document, materials such as photographs, videos, duplicates, or copies that sufficiently reflect the appearance, features, and true content of the original object or original document may be presented, along with an explanation of the reasons.

For expert opinions and records of inspections, examinations, identifications, investigative experiments, etc., the originals shall be presented.

Article 33. When the prosecution or defense presents evidence, it shall focus on content relevant to the facts of the case or content disputed by the prosecution and defense.

When presenting evidence, the content of the evidence may be presented, played, or demonstrated with the aid of multimedia devices or other means.

Article 34. If the prosecution and defense have no objection to witness testimony, victim statements, or expert opinions, and the relevant persons do not need to appear in court, or if the relevant persons cannot appear in court due to objective reasons and cannot testify through video or other means, written evidentiary materials collected before trial or audio-visual recordings of the testimony process may be presented or read out.

If the defendant’s statement in court is consistent in substance with the pre-trial statement, the pre-trial statement need not be presented again. If the defendant’s statement in court differs materially from the pre-trial statement, the parts of the pre-trial statement that contain material differences may be presented or read out.

Article 35. Evidence collected using technical investigation measures shall be presented in court. If presenting, identifying, or examining such evidence in court may endanger the personal safety of relevant persons or may cause other serious consequences, protective measures shall be taken, such as not disclosing the identity of the relevant persons or not making public the technical investigation measures and methods.

If the court decides to verify technical investigation evidence outside the courtroom, it may convene the prosecutor and defense counsel to be present. Those present shall fulfill their duty of confidentiality.

Article 36. If the court has doubts about evidence, it may notify the prosecution and defense to supplement evidence or provide explanations. If necessary, the court may, after concluding the investigation of other evidence, adjourn the trial to investigate and verify the evidence. When the court investigates and verifies evidence, it may notify the prosecution and defense to be present and shall record the verification process in the file.

Evidence supplemented by the prosecution and defense and evidence obtained by the court through out-of-court investigation and verification shall be subject to trial examination in court before it can be used as the basis for deciding the case, except for non-key evidence that does not affect conviction and sentencing and sentencing evidence favorable to the defendant, where the prosecution and defense have no objection after being consulted outside the court.

Article 37. If the prosecution or defense applies to present evidence that was not previously transferred or submitted to the People's Court before trial, and the opposing party raises an objection, the applying party shall explain the reasons. If the court, upon review, finds that the reasons are valid and that presentation is genuinely necessary, it shall grant the application.

If the opposing party needs time to prepare a defense against the new evidence, the court may announce an adjournment and determine the preparation time.

Article 38. During the trial, if the prosecution or defense applies to notify new witnesses to appear in court, to obtain new evidence, or to apply for a new expert opinion or inspection, it shall provide the basic information of the witnesses, the location of the evidence, an explanation of the facts of the case to be proved, and the reasons for requesting a new expert opinion or inspection. If the court deems it necessary, it shall grant the application and announce a postponement of the trial. If the court does not grant the application, it shall explain the reasons and continue the trial.

Article 39. During an open trial, if the prosecution or defense presents evidence involving state secrets, trade secrets, or personal privacy, the court shall stop such presentation. If the evidence is genuinely relevant to the case, the court may, based on the specific circumstances, decide to convert the case to a closed trial or to conduct the investigation of the relevant evidence in a closed session.

Article 40. During the trial, if the prosecutor discovers that the case requires supplementary investigation and recommends a postponement of the trial, the court may agree, but the recommendation for postponement shall not exceed two times.

When the People's Procuratorate transfers the supplementary collected evidence to the People's Court, the People's Court shall notify the defense counsel and agent ad litem to review, copy, or reproduce it. If the defense needs time to prepare a defense against the supplementary collected evidence, the court may announce an adjournment and determine the preparation time.

After the supplementary investigation period expires, if the People's Procuratorate, upon notification by the People's Court, does not recommend resuming the trial and does not explain the reasons, the People's Court may decide to treat the case as withdrawn by the People's Procuratorate.

Article 41. If the People's Court requests the People's Procuratorate to transfer evidentiary materials that need to be investigated and verified, or, upon application by the defendant and his or her defense counsel, requests the People's Procuratorate to transfer evidentiary materials concerning the defendant’s innocence or lesser guilt collected during the investigation or review and prosecution stages, the court shall notify the People's Procuratorate to transfer such materials within three days of receiving the decision to request evidentiary materials.

Article 42. In addition to reviewing whether the defendant has statutory sentencing circumstances, the court shall also review the following sentencing circumstances based on the circumstances of the case:

(1) The cause of the case;
(2) Whether the victim was at fault and the degree of fault, and whether the victim bears responsibility for the escalation of the conflict and the extent of that responsibility;
(3) Whether close relatives of the defendant assisted in apprehending the defendant;
(4) The defendant’s usual conduct and whether he or she shows remorse;
(5) The status of returning stolen goods, making restitution, or paying compensation;
(6) Whether the defendant has obtained forgiveness from the victim or his or her close relatives;
(7) Other circumstances affecting sentencing.

Article 43. During the trial, if the defendant or his or her defense counsel raises the existence of statutory sentencing circumstances such as voluntary surrender, truthful confession, or meritorious service, or if the People's Court discovers that the defendant may have such statutory sentencing circumstances, and the case file transferred by the People's Procuratorate does not contain relevant evidentiary materials, the court shall notify the People's Procuratorate to transfer them.

During the trial, if the defendant or his or her defense counsel raises new meritorious service circumstances and provides relevant leads or materials, the People's Court may recommend that the People's Procuratorate conduct supplementary investigation.

Article 44.
